about: The plain-English error layer (owner, 2026-11-06): every refusal or failure state the kit can show a developer, with what happened, why it matters, the exact fix and a link. Source of truth for docs/errors/ERRORS.md (python3 scripts/plain_errors.py render --write regenerates it) and for the step summaries and annotations (.github/actions/plain-errors). scripts/plain_errors.py check holds it to assurance-taxonomy.yaml: every namespace is scoped, every value of a developer namespace has an entry or is listed as not a failure.

extra_namespaces.dependabot_triage_rule: The rule that sent a Dependabot pull request to a person or closed it (.github/workflows/reusable-dependabot-triage.yml); lowercase rule ids, not taxonomy states.

scope.lineage_attribution: internal: who asserted a lineage link, recorded on ledger events for maintainers

scope.lineage_proof_failure: internal: the failure words of one kit proof, seen only by kit maintainers

routing_result.PROCEED_WITH_ADVISORY.what: The security scan passed with notes: it found things worth knowing that do not stop this change.
routing_result.PROCEED_WITH_ADVISORY.why: Nothing is blocked, but each note is a real item someone should look at before it piles up; the run summary lists them.
routing_result.PROCEED_WITH_ADVISORY.fix: Open the run summary, read "Advisory causes", and fix or ticket each one. No action is needed to merge.

routing_result.DECISION_REQUIRED.what: A person has to make a decision before this can deploy: a control was weakened without a recorded reason and owner, or an exception has expired.
routing_result.DECISION_REQUIRED.why: The kit will not guess whether a weaker control is acceptable; an unexplained weakening is a decision nobody made.
routing_result.DECISION_REQUIRED.fix: Either remove the weakening input from your workflow, or add all five fields (weakening_reason, weakening_authority, weakening_approver, weakening_exception_ref, weakening_expires) with a named approver who is not you.

routing_result.BLOCKED.what: The security scan stopped this change: a check found something that must be fixed first (for example a committed secret or a known-exploited vulnerability).
routing_result.BLOCKED.why: Merging or deploying it would ship a problem the organisation has decided must never reach production.
routing_result.BLOCKED.fix: Open the run summary, find the blocking finding (file and line), fix it in your branch and push. A committed secret must also be revoked and rotated, not just deleted.

routing_result.EVIDENCE_UNTRUSTED.what: The security scan could not finish properly, so its result cannot be trusted either way.
routing_result.EVIDENCE_UNTRUSTED.why: A scanner that did not run is not a scanner that found nothing; treating it as clean would hide real problems.
routing_result.EVIDENCE_UNTRUSTED.fix: Re-run the workflow (Actions > the run > Re-run failed jobs). If it fails the same way, the summary names the scanner and the cause; send that to the platform team.

advisory_cause.VERSION_GAP.what: No scanner the kit carries can read the language or framework version this code targets, so part of the code was not checked.
advisory_cause.VERSION_GAP.why: Unchecked code is allowed in dev and test, but uat and prod refuse it unless a named person accepts the gap.
advisory_cause.VERSION_GAP.fix: Move to a version the kit's scanners support (the summary names it), or ask AppSec to record an attributed exception before you promote to uat/prod.

advisory_cause.VERSION_GAP_UNVERIFIED.what: A scanner may not be able to read the version this code targets; nobody has measured it yet.
advisory_cause.VERSION_GAP_UNVERIFIED.why: The gap is recorded and shown, not enforced, until the kit proves the scanner's range.
advisory_cause.VERSION_GAP_UNVERIFIED.fix: Nothing to do now; if you can, move to a version listed as supported in docs/adoption/USAGE.md.

advisory_cause.COVERAGE_PARTIAL.what: A scanner checked most of the code but could not read some files (for example files with syntax it could not parse).
advisory_cause.COVERAGE_PARTIAL.why: The files it skipped were not checked, so the result covers less than the whole repository.
advisory_cause.COVERAGE_PARTIAL.fix: Open the scanner's job summary: it lists the files it could not read. Fix their syntax, or accept the gap; it does not block.

advisory_cause.WEAKENING_ATTRIBUTED.what: A control is running weaker than the kit's baseline, and a named person approved that with a reason and an expiry date.
advisory_cause.WEAKENING_ATTRIBUTED.why: Approved weakenings are allowed, but they expire; when they do, the run asks for a decision again.
advisory_cause.WEAKENING_ATTRIBUTED.fix: Nothing now. Before the expiry date, fix the cause or ask the approver to renew it.

advisory_cause.FINDINGS_NOT_BLOCKED.what: The scan found issues that do not block at this repository's current enforcement level (crawl or walk).
advisory_cause.FINDINGS_NOT_BLOCKED.why: They are real findings; at a stricter level the same findings would stop the merge.
advisory_cause.FINDINGS_NOT_BLOCKED.fix: Read the findings in the run summary and fix or ticket them while they are cheap to fix.

advisory_cause.SECRET_EXCEPTION_ATTRIBUT.what: The scan found secrets, and every one is covered by an approved, ticketed exception that has not expired.
advisory_cause.SECRET_EXCEPTION_ATTRIBUT.why: This is never a clean result: the secrets exist; a person accepted them for a time.
advisory_cause.SECRET_EXCEPTION_ATTRIBUT.fix: Rotate and remove the secrets before the exceptions expire; the exception tickets name the owner.

advisory_cause.KNOWN_EXPLOITED_EXCEPTION.what: A dependency has a vulnerability that attackers are known to exploit, and an approved, ticketed exception covers it for now.
advisory_cause.KNOWN_EXPLOITED_EXCEPTION.why: Known-exploited vulnerabilities block by default; this one passes only because a named person accepted it until a date.
advisory_cause.KNOWN_EXPLOITED_EXCEPTION.fix: Upgrade the dependency to a fixed version before the exception expires.

advisory_cause.WEAKENING_NOT_APPROVED.what: A control is weakened, but the record approving it is missing a field (reason, owner, approver, reference or expiry).
advisory_cause.WEAKENING_NOT_APPROVED.why: Below uat this is recorded; a uat or prod deploy is refused until the record is complete.
advisory_cause.WEAKENING_NOT_APPROVED.fix: Fill in all five weakening fields in the workflow inputs, with an approver who is not you.

advisory_cause.KEV_UNAVAILABLE.what: The list of known-exploited vulnerabilities (the CISA KEV catalog) could not be read on this run, so that check did not happen.
advisory_cause.KEV_UNAVAILABLE.why: The run still passes, but nobody confirmed your dependencies are free of actively exploited vulnerabilities.
advisory_cause.KEV_UNAVAILABLE.fix: Re-run later; if it persists, the platform team checks the network path to the catalog or the organisation feed mirror.

control_weakening.GATE_SOFTENED.what: A workflow input lets a scanner report without blocking (for example soft_fail_sast: true).
control_weakening.GATE_SOFTENED.why: The scanner still looks, but its findings can no longer stop a bad change.
control_weakening.GATE_SOFTENED.fix: Remove the soft-fail input from your workflow, or record why with the five weakening fields.

control_weakening.CONTROL_DISABLED.what: A workflow input switched a security check off, so it did not run.
control_weakening.CONTROL_DISABLED.why: Nothing looked at that part of the code, so problems there go unseen.
control_weakening.CONTROL_DISABLED.fix: Remove the input that disables it (the summary names it); the kit ships every check on.

control_weakening.TARGET_NOT_SUPPLIED.what: A check needs something to look at (an image or an SBOM path) and the workflow did not give it one.
control_weakening.TARGET_NOT_SUPPLIED.why: The check could not run; that part was not examined.
control_weakening.TARGET_NOT_SUPPLIED.fix: Pass the missing input the summary names, or leave it if this repository has no such artefact.

control_weakening.SCOPE_NARROWED.what: A workflow input narrowed what a check looks at (fewer paths, languages or ecosystems).
control_weakening.SCOPE_NARROWED.why: Code outside the narrowed scope was not checked.
control_weakening.SCOPE_NARROWED.fix: Remove the narrowing input, or record why with the five weakening fields.

control_weakening.SEVERITY_RAISED.what: A workflow input raised the severity at which a finding counts, so fewer findings act.
control_weakening.SEVERITY_RAISED.why: Findings below the new threshold were seen and ignored.
control_weakening.SEVERITY_RAISED.fix: Restore the default threshold, or record why with the five weakening fields.

control_weakening.CONTROL_SURFACE_DEAD.what: A workflow input you set is not read by anything, so setting it has no effect.
control_weakening.CONTROL_SURFACE_DEAD.why: You may believe a check is configured when it is not.
control_weakening.CONTROL_SURFACE_DEAD.fix: Remove the input (the summary names it) and use the one docs/adoption/USAGE.md lists.

control_weakening.WEAKENING_IN_FORCE.what: A control runs weaker than the kit's baseline on this run.
control_weakening.WEAKENING_IN_FORCE.why: A weaker control lets more through; the run records it and asks who decided.
control_weakening.WEAKENING_IN_FORCE.fix: Remove the weakening input, or add the five weakening fields with a named approver.

control_weakening.CONTROL_RECONFIGURED.what: A control's settings differ from the kit's baseline in a way the kit cannot rank as weaker or stronger.
control_weakening.CONTROL_RECONFIGURED.why: The change may weaken the check; a person should say whether it is intended.
control_weakening.CONTROL_RECONFIGURED.fix: Remove the custom setting, or record the decision with the five weakening fields.

control_weakening.WEAKENING_UNATTRIBUTED.what: A control is weakened and nobody recorded why or who decided.
control_weakening.WEAKENING_UNATTRIBUTED.why: An unexplained weakening is a decision nobody made, so the run asks for one (DECISION_REQUIRED).
control_weakening.WEAKENING_UNATTRIBUTED.fix: Add weakening_reason and weakening_authority (and the other three fields) to the workflow inputs, or remove the weakening.

control_weakening.WEAKENING_EXCEPTION_EX.what: An approved weakening has passed its expiry date.
control_weakening.WEAKENING_EXCEPTION_EX.why: Approvals never renew by silence; the run asks for a decision again.
control_weakening.WEAKENING_EXCEPTION_EX.fix: Fix the cause and remove the weakening, or ask the approver for a new expiry date.

control_weakening.WEAKENING_SELF_APPROVE.what: The person named as approver of a weakening is the person who asked for it (or the author of the change).
control_weakening.WEAKENING_SELF_APPROVE.why: Approving your own exception is never accepted: the gate blocks and every deploy refuses.
control_weakening.WEAKENING_SELF_APPROVE.fix: Ask someone on the approver list who is not you to approve it, and put their name in weakening_approver.

policy_resolution.POLICY_REGISTER_CONFLI.what: Two policy entries disagree about the same thing, so the kit cannot tell which one applies.
policy_resolution.POLICY_REGISTER_CONFLI.why: Picking one by file order would be an accident, not a decision.
policy_resolution.POLICY_REGISTER_CONFLI.fix: Ask the policy owner to remove one of the two entries the summary names (in .security/policy-registration.json or the central register).

policy_resolution.POLICY_DECISION_UNATTR.what: A policy entry has no recorded owner, reason, decision date or expiry.
policy_resolution.POLICY_DECISION_UNATTR.why: Every policy is a decision by a named person; an unsigned one is refused.
policy_resolution.POLICY_DECISION_UNATTR.fix: Ask the policy owner to add the decision fields (authority, reason, decided_on, expires) to the entry the summary names.

policy_resolution.POLICY_DECISION_EXPIRE.what: A policy entry that applies to this run has passed its expiry date.
policy_resolution.POLICY_DECISION_EXPIRE.why: Any loosening it gave is withdrawn until someone renews or replaces it.
policy_resolution.POLICY_DECISION_EXPIRE.fix: Ask the policy owner to renew the entry (new expires date) or remove it.

policy_resolution.REPOSITORY_FILE_SOFTEN.what: This repository's own policy file tries to make a check weaker than the organisation's policy allows.
policy_resolution.REPOSITORY_FILE_SOFTEN.why: A repository may make its policy stricter, never looser; the loosening is ignored and the run blocks.
policy_resolution.REPOSITORY_FILE_SOFTEN.fix: Remove the loosening from .security/policy-registration.json, or ask the central policy owner for the change.

policy_resolution.POLICY_BELOW_AUTHORITY.what: A policy entry for a narrower scope (team, product, repository) tries to go below what a broader scope set.
policy_resolution.POLICY_BELOW_AUTHORITY.why: Narrower scopes may only tighten; the floor holds and the run blocks.
policy_resolution.POLICY_BELOW_AUTHORITY.fix: Ask the policy owner to raise the entry to at least the floor the summary names.

policy_resolution.ORG_NOT_UNDER_ENTERPRI.what: This refusal is retired and no longer emitted.
policy_resolution.ORG_NOT_UNDER_ENTERPRI.why: It is kept only because older records name it.
policy_resolution.ORG_NOT_UNDER_ENTERPRI.fix: Nothing to do; if you see it, the kit version is old: update the pinned kit SHA.

policy_resolution.EXCEPTION_RENEWAL_LIMI.what: An exception has been renewed more times than the policy allows.
policy_resolution.EXCEPTION_RENEWAL_LIMI.why: Endless renewals hide a problem; the exception is refused and the finding is treated normally again.
policy_resolution.EXCEPTION_RENEWAL_LIMI.fix: Fix the underlying finding; a further exception needs the policy owner to decide, not another renewal.

policy_resolution.EXCEPTION_HISTORY_TAMP.what: An exception claims fewer renewals than the git history of the policy file shows.
policy_resolution.EXCEPTION_HISTORY_TAMP.why: The recorded history must match what actually happened; the exception is refused and the run blocks.
policy_resolution.EXCEPTION_HISTORY_TAMP.fix: Correct the exception's renewal history to match git (the summary shows the count) and have it re-approved.

policy_resolution.EXCEPTION_HISTORY_UNVE.what: The kit could not read the git history of the policy file, so it cannot check how often an exception was renewed.
policy_resolution.EXCEPTION_HISTORY_UNVE.why: An unreadable history is never treated as zero renewals; the exception does not apply.
policy_resolution.EXCEPTION_HISTORY_UNVE.fix: Check out with full history (actions/checkout fetch-depth: 0) or ask the platform team; then re-run.

policy_resolution.POLICY_MODE_SUPPLIED.what: The workflow passed a policy mode as an input; the kit derives it and never accepts it from a caller.
policy_resolution.POLICY_MODE_SUPPLIED.why: A derived value that a caller can override is not a control.
policy_resolution.POLICY_MODE_SUPPLIED.fix: Remove the policy_mode input from your workflow; set enforcement through the policy register instead.

policy_resolution.TICKET_ROUTING_BELOW_F.what: A policy entry routes secrets, known-exploited or malicious-package findings to "no ticket".
policy_resolution.TICKET_ROUTING_BELOW_F.why: Those findings must always be ticketed somewhere; switching them off is refused.
policy_resolution.TICKET_ROUTING_BELOW_F.fix: Route them to a real project in the policy entry the summary names.

policy_resolution.CHERRY_PICK_BELOW_FLOO.what: The policy (or a workflow input) asks for less than the kit's minimum: a secret check below blocking, or a required scan switched off.
policy_resolution.CHERRY_PICK_BELOW_FLOO.why: Secret, known-exploited and malicious-package checks always block; nobody can switch them off.
policy_resolution.CHERRY_PICK_BELOW_FLOO.fix: Remove the setting the summary names (for example enable_malicious_pkg_scan: false) from the policy or the workflow.

policy_resolution.CELLS_NOT_MONOTONE.what: The policy makes a lower environment stricter than a higher one (for example dev stricter than prod).
policy_resolution.CELLS_NOT_MONOTONE.why: Enforcement must grow along the promotion path, or problems are found weeks later at the last gate.
policy_resolution.CELLS_NOT_MONOTONE.fix: Ask the policy owner to order the rungs so dev <= test <= uat = prod.

policy_resolution.CELL_NOT_REGISTERED.what: The policy file has no entry for the environment this run is checked for.
policy_resolution.CELL_NOT_REGISTERED.why: Without an entry there is no floor to apply, so the result cannot be trusted.
policy_resolution.CELL_NOT_REGISTERED.fix: Add an entry for the environment the summary names, or map the environment name to a tier in environment_names.

policy_resolution.REGISTRATION_UNAVAILAB.what: The policy file could not be read (invalid JSON, wrong schema, or the protected branch could not be reached).
policy_resolution.REGISTRATION_UNAVAILAB.why: An unreadable policy is not the default policy; the run cannot decide.
policy_resolution.REGISTRATION_UNAVAILAB.fix: Validate .security/policy-registration.json against the schema (python3 scripts/policy_registration.py --validate .security/policy-registration.json --origin repository) and fix the error it names.

policy_resolution.POLICY_NUMBER_NOT_CONF.what: A number the policy needs (a count, a period, a grace time) is missing from the policy file.
policy_resolution.POLICY_NUMBER_NOT_CONF.why: The kit never invents a number on the owner's behalf.
policy_resolution.POLICY_NUMBER_NOT_CONF.fix: Ask the policy owner to add the number the summary names to the register's numbers block.

policy_notice.ORG_UNMAPPED_RAN_AT_ENTERP.what: This organisation is not named in the central policy, so the run used the enterprise minimum.
policy_notice.ORG_UNMAPPED_RAN_AT_ENTERP.why: You are checked at the safe floor; your organisation's own policy was not applied.
policy_notice.ORG_UNMAPPED_RAN_AT_ENTERP.fix: Ask the policy owner to add this organisation to the central register's orgs map.

policy_notice.ORG_UNMAPPED_RAN_AT_STRICT.what: This organisation is not known to the central policy, so the run used the strictest registered organisation's rules.
policy_notice.ORG_UNMAPPED_RAN_AT_STRICT.why: You are checked strictly until someone registers your organisation.
policy_notice.ORG_UNMAPPED_RAN_AT_STRICT.fix: Ask the policy owner to register this organisation in the central register.

secret_exception_refusal.SECRET_EXCEPTIO.what: A secret exception does not name exactly one finding (its 12-character fingerprint).
secret_exception_refusal.SECRET_EXCEPTIO.why: An exception must cover one known secret, never a pattern; the secret still blocks.
secret_exception_refusal.SECRET_EXCEPTIO.fix: Put the finding's fingerprint (fp in the scan report) in the exception.

secret_exception_refusal.SECRET_EXCEPTIO.what: A secret exception has no valid work-item ticket (PROJECT-1234).
secret_exception_refusal.SECRET_EXCEPTIO.why: Every exception must be traceable to a ticket; the secret still blocks.
secret_exception_refusal.SECRET_EXCEPTIO.fix: Add the ticket key to the exception's ticket field.

secret_exception_refusal.SECRET_EXCEPTIO.what: A secret exception is missing its explanation, approver or expiry (or, at uat/prod, the environment reviewers).
secret_exception_refusal.SECRET_EXCEPTIO.why: An exception nobody explained or approved is not an exception; the secret still blocks.
secret_exception_refusal.SECRET_EXCEPTIO.fix: Fill in explanation, approver, expires (and environment_reviewers for uat/prod).

secret_exception_refusal.SECRET_EXCEPTIO.what: A secret exception has passed its expiry date.
secret_exception_refusal.SECRET_EXCEPTIO.why: Exceptions never renew by silence; the secret blocks again.
secret_exception_refusal.SECRET_EXCEPTIO.fix: Rotate and remove the secret, or ask the approver for a new expiry.

known_exploited.UNAVAILABLE.what: The known-exploited vulnerability check could not run: the catalog could not be fetched or read.
known_exploited.UNAVAILABLE.why: Nobody confirmed your dependencies are free of actively exploited vulnerabilities on this run.
known_exploited.UNAVAILABLE.fix: Re-run later; if it persists, the platform team checks the network path to the catalog or the feed mirror.

known_exploited.EXCEPTED.what: A dependency has a known-exploited vulnerability that an approved, ticketed exception covers for now.
known_exploited.EXCEPTED.why: It is not clean: attackers use this vulnerability; a named person accepted it until a date.
known_exploited.EXCEPTED.fix: Upgrade the dependency to a fixed version before the exception expires.

known_exploited.FINDING_KNOWN_EXPLOITED.what: A dependency or image contains a vulnerability that attackers are actively exploiting (it is on the CISA KEV list).
known_exploited.FINDING_KNOWN_EXPLOITED.why: This always blocks, at every enforcement level: it is the kind of flaw used in real attacks today.
known_exploited.FINDING_KNOWN_EXPLOITED.fix: Upgrade the package to the fixed version the finding names (Dependabot may already have a pull request), then push.

known_exploited_exception_refusal.KEV_EX.what: A known-exploited exception does not name exactly one finding and one CVE.
known_exploited_exception_refusal.KEV_EX.why: A blanket exception is never accepted; the vulnerability still blocks.
known_exploited_exception_refusal.KEV_EX.fix: Name the finding fingerprint and the CVE in the exception.

known_exploited_exception_refusal.KEV_EX.what: A known-exploited exception has no valid work-item ticket.
known_exploited_exception_refusal.KEV_EX.why: Every exception must be traceable; the vulnerability still blocks.
known_exploited_exception_refusal.KEV_EX.fix: Add the ticket key (PROJECT-1234) to the exception.

known_exploited_exception_refusal.KEV_EX.what: A known-exploited exception is missing its explanation, approver, expiry or reviewers, or its history cannot be read.
known_exploited_exception_refusal.KEV_EX.why: An unexplained exception is refused; the vulnerability still blocks.
known_exploited_exception_refusal.KEV_EX.fix: Fill in the missing fields the summary names.

known_exploited_exception_refusal.KEV_EX.what: A known-exploited exception has passed its expiry date.
known_exploited_exception_refusal.KEV_EX.fix: Upgrade the dependency, or ask the approver for a new expiry.

feed_mirror.MIRROR_STALE.what: The organisation's copy of a vulnerability database has not been refreshed recently enough.
feed_mirror.MIRROR_STALE.why: Old data cannot show your dependencies are free of newly published vulnerabilities, so it is not used.
feed_mirror.MIRROR_STALE.fix: Tell the platform team: the feed-mirror refresh workflow has stopped (they re-run reusable-feed-mirror-refresh.yml).

feed_mirror.MIRROR_UNREACHABLE.what: The organisation's copy of a vulnerability database could not be reached from this runner.
feed_mirror.MIRROR_UNREACHABLE.why: A database that cannot be read is not a clean result.
feed_mirror.MIRROR_UNREACHABLE.fix: Run the job on a runner with access to the mirror (vars.KIT_FEED_MIRROR_RUNNER), or ask the platform team to check the private endpoint.

feed_mirror.MIRROR_INTEGRITY_FAILED.what: The organisation's copy of a vulnerability database failed its integrity check (a file does not match its checksum).
feed_mirror.MIRROR_INTEGRITY_FAILED.why: Corrupt or tampered data is never used.
feed_mirror.MIRROR_INTEGRITY_FAILED.fix: Tell the platform team; they re-run the mirror refresh and investigate the mismatch.

feed_mirror.MIRROR_FALLBACK_UPSTREAM.what: The organisation's mirror was refused, and the public feed was read instead because the repository allows that fallback.
feed_mirror.MIRROR_FALLBACK_UPSTREAM.why: This is an approved exception to the private-only rule; it is recorded so it gets reviewed.
feed_mirror.MIRROR_FALLBACK_UPSTREAM.fix: Nothing to do now; the platform team fixes the mirror (the summary names its cause).

feed_mirror_refresh.MIRROR_UPSTREAM_STAL.what: The public vulnerability database itself is older than allowed, so the mirror was not updated from it.
feed_mirror_refresh.MIRROR_UPSTREAM_STAL.why: Publishing old data would reset the freshness clock over stale content.
feed_mirror_refresh.MIRROR_UPSTREAM_STAL.fix: Re-run the refresh later; if it persists, check the upstream feed's status page.

feed_mirror_refresh.MIRROR_UPSTREAM_UNRE.what: The public vulnerability database could not be downloaded.
feed_mirror_refresh.MIRROR_UPSTREAM_UNRE.why: The mirror keeps its last good copy, which will go stale if this continues.
feed_mirror_refresh.MIRROR_UPSTREAM_UNRE.fix: Re-run the refresh; if it persists, check the runner's outbound network access.

feed_mirror_refresh.MIRROR_UPSTREAM_INTE.what: The downloaded vulnerability database does not match its own published checksums.
feed_mirror_refresh.MIRROR_UPSTREAM_INTE.why: Corrupt data is never published to the mirror.
feed_mirror_refresh.MIRROR_UPSTREAM_INTE.fix: Re-run the refresh; if it persists, report it to the platform team.

feed_mirror_refresh.MIRROR_PUBLISH_UNVER.what: The mirror was uploaded, but reading it back did not show a current, intact copy.
feed_mirror_refresh.MIRROR_PUBLISH_UNVER.why: A publish nobody could read back is not a working mirror.
feed_mirror_refresh.MIRROR_PUBLISH_UNVER.fix: Check the storage account and the private endpoint, then re-run the refresh.

scanner_state.PARTIAL.what: A scanner ran but something it needed was missing, so it could not check everything.
scanner_state.PARTIAL.why: What it skipped is unchecked; the result is not a clean bill of health.
scanner_state.PARTIAL.fix: Open the scanner's job summary for the missing prerequisite (a build file, a lockfile, a version) and add it.

scanner_state.FAILED.what: A scanner crashed or exited with an error.
scanner_state.FAILED.why: Its findings were not established, so the run cannot be trusted as clean.
scanner_state.FAILED.fix: Re-run the failed job; if it fails again, send the job log to the platform team.

scanner_state.COLLECTION_FAILED.what: A scanner ran, but its results could not be collected (the report was empty or unreadable).
scanner_state.COLLECTION_FAILED.why: An empty report looks exactly like a clean scan, so the kit refuses to treat it as one.
scanner_state.COLLECTION_FAILED.fix: Re-run the job; if it repeats, it is a pipeline defect: send the job log to the platform team.

scanner_state.UNAVAILABLE.what: A scanner never ran on this run.
scanner_state.UNAVAILABLE.why: Nothing was checked by it, so the run cannot say the code is clean.
scanner_state.UNAVAILABLE.fix: The summary gives the reason (a download failure, a timeout, a licence); re-run, or pass the reason to the platform team.

execution_unavailable_reason.BILLING_EXE.what: GitHub refused to run the job because of a spending limit or a payment problem.
execution_unavailable_reason.BILLING_EXE.why: No scanner ran, so nothing was checked.
execution_unavailable_reason.BILLING_EXE.fix: Ask an organisation owner to check Settings > Billing (Actions spending limit), then re-run.

execution_unavailable_reason.ACTION_ACQU.what: The runner could not download an action the job needs.
execution_unavailable_reason.ACTION_ACQU.why: The job never started its checks.
execution_unavailable_reason.ACTION_ACQU.fix: Re-run; if it persists, check that the organisation allows the action (Settings > Actions > General) and that the kit repository is accessible to this one.

execution_unavailable_reason.POLICY_REFU.what: An environment protection rule refused to run the job on this branch or ref.
execution_unavailable_reason.POLICY_REFU.why: The job was stopped before it ran.
execution_unavailable_reason.POLICY_REFU.fix: Run it from a branch the environment allows (usually main), or ask an admin to check the environment's deployment branch policy.

execution_unavailable_reason.EXECUTION_T.what: The job ran out of time and was stopped.
execution_unavailable_reason.EXECUTION_T.why: The scan did not finish, so its result is unknown.
execution_unavailable_reason.EXECUTION_T.fix: Re-run; if it times out again, the repository may be very large: ask the platform team about the timeout or the scan scope.

execution_unavailable_reason.DEPENDENCY_.what: A tool the scanner needs could not be downloaded or did not work.
execution_unavailable_reason.DEPENDENCY_.fix: Re-run; if it persists, send the job log to the platform team (often a blocked download or a changed checksum).

execution_unavailable_reason.DISCOVERY_U.what: The kit could not work out which languages and files this repository has.
execution_unavailable_reason.DISCOVERY_U.why: Without that, every scanner runs, which is slower but safe; nothing is skipped as "not applicable".
execution_unavailable_reason.DISCOVERY_U.fix: Re-run; if it persists, send the discover job's log to the platform team.

execution_unavailable_reason.INFRASTRUCT.what: A scanner never ran, for a reason the kit could not identify.
execution_unavailable_reason.INFRASTRUCT.fix: Re-run; if it repeats, send the job log to the platform team.

prerequisite_readiness.PREREQUISITE_UNAV.what: A tool a check needs is missing on this runner, and the kit has no way to install it.
prerequisite_readiness.PREREQUISITE_UNAV.fix: Run on a GitHub-hosted runner (ubuntu-latest) or ask the platform team to add the tool to your runner.

prerequisite_readiness.ACQUISITION_UNAVA.what: The kit tried to install a tool a check needs and could not.
prerequisite_readiness.ACQUISITION_UNAVA.fix: Re-run; if it persists, check the runner's network access to the tool's download site.

prerequisite_readiness.FITNESS_FAILED.what: A tool is installed but does not work (it failed its self-check).
prerequisite_readiness.FITNESS_FAILED.why: A broken tool would give a meaningless result, so the check does not run.
prerequisite_readiness.FITNESS_FAILED.fix: Re-run on a fresh runner; if it persists, report the tool and version in the log to the platform team.

prerequisite_readiness.REMEDIATION_FAILE.what: The kit installed a missing tool, but it still does not work.
prerequisite_readiness.REMEDIATION_FAILE.fix: Send the job log to the platform team.

capability_floor_state.GAP_DECIDED.what: A required scanner was removed under an approved, time-limited decision, and nothing replaces it yet.
capability_floor_state.GAP_DECIDED.why: That coverage is missing on purpose for now; it does not block.
capability_floor_state.GAP_DECIDED.fix: Nothing for you; the platform team owns the replacement before the decision expires.

capability_floor_state.BREACHED.what: A scanner that every run must include produced no result, or was removed without a recorded decision.
capability_floor_state.BREACHED.why: The kit refuses to report on a run missing a required check.
capability_floor_state.BREACHED.fix: Re-run; if it persists, the kit copy may be broken or out of date: update the pinned kit SHA or tell the platform team.

api_token_preflight.JOB_TOKEN_REJECTED.what: GitHub rejected the workflow's own token (401 Bad credentials).
api_token_preflight.JOB_TOKEN_REJECTED.why: Every check that reads GitHub (branch protection, environments, alerts) cannot run.
api_token_preflight.JOB_TOKEN_REJECTED.fix: If the error URL names api.github.com on a <tenant>.ghe.com host, update the pinned kit SHA (KDEC-027); otherwise an organisation owner checks the IP allow list and Actions permissions.

api_token_preflight.ORG_IP_ALLOW_LIST_BL.what: The organisation's IP allow list blocks this runner from calling GitHub.
api_token_preflight.ORG_IP_ALLOW_LIST_BL.why: The checks that read GitHub cannot run; it is a platform setting, not your code.
api_token_preflight.ORG_IP_ALLOW_LIST_BL.fix: An organisation owner allows GitHub-hosted runners (Settings > Security > IP allow list > allow GitHub Actions) or uses a listed runner.

api_token_preflight.ORG_SSO_BLOCKS_TOKEN.what: Single sign-on blocked a token, which means a step used a personal or app token instead of the workflow's own token.
api_token_preflight.ORG_SSO_BLOCKS_TOKEN.why: The workflow's own token is exempt from SSO; a personal token needs SSO authorisation.
api_token_preflight.ORG_SSO_BLOCKS_TOKEN.fix: Remove the personal token from GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN in your workflow, or authorise it for SSO.

api_token_preflight.RATE_LIMITED.what: GitHub rate-limited the workflow's API calls.
api_token_preflight.RATE_LIMITED.why: Checks it stopped are unknown, never passed.
api_token_preflight.RATE_LIMITED.fix: Wait for the limit to reset (the log shows when) and re-run.

api_token_preflight.API_UNREACHABLE.what: The runner could not reach the GitHub API at all (DNS, connection or timeout).
api_token_preflight.API_UNREACHABLE.why: No check that reads GitHub could run.
api_token_preflight.API_UNREACHABLE.fix: Re-run; if it persists on a self-hosted runner, its administrator checks outbound access to the API host.

api_token_preflight.TOKEN_PREFLIGHT_UNCL.what: GitHub refused the workflow's token for a reason the kit does not recognise (a missing scope, a 404, a server error).
api_token_preflight.TOKEN_PREFLIGHT_UNCL.why: The checks that read GitHub cannot be trusted.
api_token_preflight.TOKEN_PREFLIGHT_UNCL.fix: Read the step log for the HTTP status; most often the job's permissions: block lacks a scope. Compare it with the template.

scan_partial_reason.PARSE_PARTIAL_PHP_SY.what: Semgrep could not parse some PHP files, so those files were not checked; everything else was.
scan_partial_reason.PARSE_PARTIAL_PHP_SY.why: Syntax it cannot read may hide a vulnerability.
scan_partial_reason.PARSE_PARTIAL_PHP_SY.fix: Open the sast-semgrep summary for the file list; fix the syntax or accept the gap (it does not block).

scan_partial_reason.CPP_ANALYSIS_PARTIAL.what: Some C/C++ files could not be analysed because the kit found no build information for them.
scan_partial_reason.CPP_ANALYSIS_PARTIAL.why: The kit never invents a build system, so those files were not checked.
scan_partial_reason.CPP_ANALYSIS_PARTIAL.fix: Commit a compile_commands.json, or a top-level CMakeLists.txt or Makefile the kit can read.

scan_partial_reason.CODEQL_BUILD_PARTIAL.what: CodeQL's automatic build did not fully succeed, so part of the code may not have been analysed.
scan_partial_reason.CODEQL_BUILD_PARTIAL.why: An unknown part of the code went unchecked.
scan_partial_reason.CODEQL_BUILD_PARTIAL.fix: Make the project build with its standard command on ubuntu-latest (the CodeQL job log shows the build error).

scan_examination.EXAMINED_NOTHING.what: A scanner reported success but, by its own account, examined nothing.
scan_examination.EXAMINED_NOTHING.why: Zero findings from a scanner that read nothing is not a clean result.
scan_examination.EXAMINED_NOTHING.fix: Open the scanner's summary: usually the files could not be parsed or no file matched; fix that and re-run.

scan_examination.NOT_DECLARED.what: A scanner's report does not say what it examined.
scan_examination.NOT_DECLARED.why: The kit cannot count it as a clean scan.
scan_examination.NOT_DECLARED.fix: Re-run; if it repeats, report the scanner and its version to the platform team.

artifact_identity.IDENTITY_UNVERIFIED.what: The image was pushed, but the kit could not prove the pushed image is the one it scanned.
artifact_identity.IDENTITY_UNVERIFIED.why: Deploying an image nobody can tie to its scan would ship unchecked bytes; deploys are refused.
artifact_identity.IDENTITY_UNVERIFIED.fix: Re-run the build; if it repeats, check the registry login and that nothing else pushes the same tag.

artifact_identity.NOT_ESTABLISHED.what: The build never got far enough to establish which image it produced.
artifact_identity.NOT_ESTABLISHED.fix: Fix the earlier failure in the build job and re-run.

artifact_identity.SITE_DIGEST_MISMATCH.what: The static site about to be released is not byte-for-byte the one that was checked and approved.
artifact_identity.SITE_DIGEST_MISMATCH.why: A changed, added or renamed file is a different release; nothing was deployed.
artifact_identity.SITE_DIGEST_MISMATCH.fix: Re-run the workflow from the merge so the package, attestation and deploy come from the same build.

leak_gate_state.OFF.what: One of the layers that stop a committed secret reaching main is switched off.
leak_gate_state.OFF.why: Secrets get one fewer chance to be caught before they land.
leak_gate_state.OFF.fix: Turn the named layer on (push protection or the push ruleset); docs/adoption/LEAK_GATES.md has the exact steps.

leak_gate_state.UNKNOWN.what: The kit could not read whether a secret-protection layer is on (this token cannot see it).
leak_gate_state.UNKNOWN.why: Unknown is neither on nor off; nobody knows.
leak_gate_state.UNKNOWN.fix: Ask a repository admin to confirm the layer in Settings > Code security, or grant the read the summary names.

leak_gate_state.NO_LEAK_GATE_SHOWN.what: Only the CI secret scan stands between a committed secret and main: no other protection could be shown on.
leak_gate_state.NO_LEAK_GATE_SHOWN.why: A secret is caught only after it is already pushed.
leak_gate_state.NO_LEAK_GATE_SHOWN.fix: Turn on push protection or apply the kit's push ruleset (docs/adoption/LEAK_GATES.md steps 1-3).

leak_gate_setup_refusal.NOT_APPLIED.what: GitHub refused to create the push ruleset (no admin rights, or the plan does not support rulesets).
leak_gate_setup_refusal.NOT_APPLIED.why: The layer is not in place.
leak_gate_setup_refusal.NOT_APPLIED.fix: Run apply-push-ruleset.sh as a repository admin; on a personal or unlicensed repository, rulesets are not available.

leak_gate_setup_refusal.REPO_NOT_READABL.what: The ruleset helper could not read the repository (wrong name, wrong host, or no access).
leak_gate_setup_refusal.REPO_NOT_READABL.fix: Check OWNER/REPO and GH_HOST (a <tenant>.ghe.com repository needs GH_HOST set), and that your token can read it.

leak_gate_setup_refusal.RULESET_LOOKUP_F.what: The helper could not list the repository's rulesets, so it does not know whether the kit's ruleset exists.
leak_gate_setup_refusal.RULESET_LOOKUP_F.why: Creating one blindly could duplicate it; nothing was done.
leak_gate_setup_refusal.RULESET_LOOKUP_F.fix: Re-run with a token that can read rulesets (repository administration read).

leak_gate_setup_refusal.TEMPLATE_UNREADA.what: The kit's push-ruleset file next to the helper is missing or broken.
leak_gate_setup_refusal.TEMPLATE_UNREADA.why: There is nothing to apply; the kit copy is damaged.
leak_gate_setup_refusal.TEMPLATE_UNREADA.fix: Re-fetch the kit at its pinned SHA and run again.

leak_gate_setup_refusal.BASELINE_UNREADA.what: The kit's baseline .gitignore next to the helper is missing or empty.
leak_gate_setup_refusal.BASELINE_UNREADA.why: There is nothing to merge; the kit copy is damaged.
leak_gate_setup_refusal.BASELINE_UNREADA.fix: Re-fetch the kit at its pinned SHA and run again.

leak_gate_setup_refusal.REPO_DIR_MISSING.what: The directory given to merge-baseline.sh does not exist.
leak_gate_setup_refusal.REPO_DIR_MISSING.fix: Pass the path of your repository's root folder.

leak_gate_setup_refusal.NOT_A_GIT_REPO.what: The directory given to merge-baseline.sh is not a git repository.
leak_gate_setup_refusal.NOT_A_GIT_REPO.why: A .gitignore outside a repository protects nothing.
leak_gate_setup_refusal.NOT_A_GIT_REPO.fix: Pass the root folder of a git clone.

leak_gate_setup_refusal.TARGET_NOT_WRITA.what: The repository's .gitignore could not be written.
leak_gate_setup_refusal.TARGET_NOT_WRITA.why: The baseline patterns are not (all) in place.
leak_gate_setup_refusal.TARGET_NOT_WRITA.fix: Make .gitignore writable (check its permissions or a lock) and re-run; the merge completes without duplicates.

leak_gate_setup_refusal.MERGE_NOT_VERIFI.what: After writing .gitignore, at least one baseline pattern is still missing.
leak_gate_setup_refusal.MERGE_NOT_VERIFI.why: Success is claimed only for what the file really contains.
leak_gate_setup_refusal.MERGE_NOT_VERIFI.fix: Re-run merge-baseline.sh; it names each missing pattern on stderr.

platform_applicability.UNAVAILABLE.what: A check is not available to this repository (not licensed, or the feature is off for the organisation).
platform_applicability.UNAVAILABLE.why: That check could not run; it is a platform decision, not something your code did.
platform_applicability.UNAVAILABLE.fix: Nothing for you; the platform team decides whether to license or replace it (on GHE.com with GHAS off, CodeQL is not graded).

platform_applicability.NOT_CONFIGURED.what: A check is available but switched off for this repository.
platform_applicability.NOT_CONFIGURED.why: It did not run; someone chose that, or never chose.
platform_applicability.NOT_CONFIGURED.fix: Ask a repository admin whether it should be on (the summary names the setting).

platform_applicability.UNKNOWN.what: The kit could not tell whether a check applies here (the token could not see the setting).
platform_applicability.UNKNOWN.why: The check runs anyway, and the result says so.
platform_applicability.UNKNOWN.fix: Nothing for you; an admin can confirm the setting.

execution_state.FAILED.what: A scanner job did not finish.
execution_state.FAILED.fix: Re-run the job; if it fails again, send its log to the platform team.

execution_state.NOT_RUN.what: A scanner job never started (skipped, cancelled or gated off earlier in the run).
execution_state.NOT_RUN.fix: Look for the earlier job that failed or was cancelled, fix it, and re-run.

execution_state.NOT_DECLARED.what: A scanner job did not say whether it completed.
execution_state.NOT_DECLARED.why: The kit never assumes a job completed.
execution_state.NOT_DECLARED.fix: Re-run; if it repeats, report the job name to the platform team.

deploy_coverage.NO_KIT_ADAPTER.what: This repository deploys to a kind of hosting the kit has no deploy step for (for example AKS, VMs or code-packaged Functions).
deploy_coverage.NO_KIT_ADAPTER.why: The kit scans the code, but its deploy safety checks do not cover that hosting.
deploy_coverage.NO_KIT_ADAPTER.fix: Deploy as a container (Container Apps or App Service) or a static site, or ask the platform team about your hosting.

publication_state.PUBLICATION_DEGRADED.what: A place results are shown (such as the Security tab) was not available, so results were not published there.
publication_state.PUBLICATION_DEGRADED.why: The scan itself still counts; only the display is missing. An empty Security tab is not a clean codebase.
publication_state.PUBLICATION_DEGRADED.fix: Read the results in the run summary and the evidence artifact instead.

publication_state.NO_FINDINGS_COUNT.what: The report job finished but published no count of blocking findings.
publication_state.NO_FINDINGS_COUNT.why: No count is not a count of zero; the run cannot pass.
publication_state.NO_FINDINGS_COUNT.fix: Re-run; if it repeats, send the report job's log to the platform team.

discovery_state.EXCLUDED_BY_SELECTOR.what: Code of a kind the kit scans is present, but a workflow input excluded it.
discovery_state.EXCLUDED_BY_SELECTOR.fix: Remove the exclusion input, or record why with the five weakening fields.

discovery_state.DISABLED.what: A check was explicitly turned off for this repository.
discovery_state.DISABLED.why: It is an exception, and it is reported every run.
discovery_state.DISABLED.fix: Turn it back on, or make sure the exception is recorded with an owner and expiry.

discovery_state.MISSING_BUT_REQUIRED.what: Something this repository is declared to have (for example infrastructure code) is missing.
discovery_state.MISSING_BUT_REQUIRED.why: The absence itself is the finding.
discovery_state.MISSING_BUT_REQUIRED.fix: Add the missing part, or correct the declaration (for example iac_mode) in the workflow.

discovery_state.SCANNER_UNAVAILABLE.what: The kit has no scanner for a kind of file found in this repository.
discovery_state.SCANNER_UNAVAILABLE.why: That code was not checked by anything.
discovery_state.SCANNER_UNAVAILABLE.fix: Nothing for you; the platform team owns adding a scanner (the summary names the kind).

discovery_state.COVERAGE_GAP.what: Code is present that needs a check, and no scanner looked at it.
discovery_state.COVERAGE_GAP.why: This is neither clean nor not-applicable: it is unchecked.
discovery_state.COVERAGE_GAP.fix: Tell the platform team which kind of file it is (the summary names it); consider a scanner or a manual review.

discovery_state.UNDETERMINED_PRESENT.what: The kit could not tell whether code of one kind is present, so it scans for it anyway.
discovery_state.UNDETERMINED_PRESENT.why: An unknown is never treated as absent.
discovery_state.UNDETERMINED_PRESENT.fix: Nothing for you; re-run if the discover job failed.

discovery_state.DISCOVERY_PARTIAL.what: Some of the kit's file-type probes failed; the rest worked.
discovery_state.DISCOVERY_PARTIAL.why: The probes that failed are treated as present, so those scanners run anyway.
discovery_state.DISCOVERY_PARTIAL.fix: Re-run; if it persists, send the discover job's log to the platform team.

coverage_state.UNSUPPORTED_PRESENT.what: This repository has code in a language the kit has no scanner for, and it was not scanned.
coverage_state.UNSUPPORTED_PRESENT.fix: Ask the platform team whether a scanner exists for it; until then, review it by hand.

coverage_state.COVERAGE_UNDETERMINED.what: The kit could not work out how much of the code it can check.
coverage_state.COVERAGE_UNDETERMINED.fix: Re-run; if it persists, send the discover job's log to the platform team.

version_applicability.VERSION_UNSUPPORTE.what: A scanner cannot read the language version this code targets.
version_applicability.VERSION_UNSUPPORTE.why: That scanner's part was not checked; another may substitute.
version_applicability.VERSION_UNSUPPORTE.fix: Move to a supported version (docs/adoption/USAGE.md lists them) or accept the advisory.

version_applicability.VERSION_SUPPORT_UN.what: The kit could not tell whether a scanner can read the language version this code targets.
version_applicability.VERSION_SUPPORT_UN.why: The result for that part is uncertain.
version_applicability.VERSION_SUPPORT_UN.fix: Pin the version explicitly (for example .python-version, global.json, go.mod's go line) so the kit can read it.

version_applicability.PLATFORM_UNAVAILAB.what: A scanner that could read this code was withdrawn by the platform on this repository (for example code scanning unavailable).
version_applicability.PLATFORM_UNAVAILAB.why: That check did not run; it is a platform decision.
version_applicability.PLATFORM_UNAVAILAB.fix: Nothing for you; the platform team decides.

api_boundary.UNDETERMINED.what: The kit could not establish the security posture: something it needed did not run or could not be collected.
api_boundary.UNDETERMINED.fix: Re-run; the summary names what was unavailable.

api_boundary.ADVISORY.what: Findings existed and were deliberately not blocked at this enforcement level.
api_boundary.ADVISORY.why: They are real; at a stricter level they would block.
api_boundary.ADVISORY.fix: Read and fix or ticket them.

api_boundary.UNBOUND.what: The evidence could not be tied to the exact commit and run that produced it.
api_boundary.UNBOUND.why: Unbound evidence must not be merged or compared with other runs.
api_boundary.UNBOUND.fix: Re-run; if it repeats, report it to the platform team.

finding_baseline_state.BASELINE_UNAVAILA.what: The record of findings that already existed (the baseline ledger) could not be read.
finding_baseline_state.BASELINE_UNAVAILA.why: The kit cannot tell new findings from old ones, so it treats them all as new.
finding_baseline_state.BASELINE_UNAVAILA.fix: Check the ledger file on the default branch is valid JSON; re-run.

remediation_track_state.BREACHED_UNDECID.what: A known finding is past its fix deadline and nobody has decided what to do.
remediation_track_state.BREACHED_UNDECID.why: Overdue findings owe a decision; after the grace period they block.
remediation_track_state.BREACHED_UNDECID.fix: Fix it, or ask its owner to record a dated decision.

remediation_track_state.TRACK_STALLED.what: No known finding in this repository has been fixed in the configured period.
remediation_track_state.TRACK_STALLED.why: A schedule nobody follows is not remediation.
remediation_track_state.TRACK_STALLED.fix: Fix at least the oldest findings; the promotion review asks for a decision.

remediation_track_state.TRACK_NOT_ADMITT.what: A known finding is not on a fix schedule (no fix status, severity or deadline recorded).
remediation_track_state.TRACK_NOT_ADMITT.why: It cannot be tracked to closure.
remediation_track_state.TRACK_NOT_ADMITT.fix: Ask the finding's owner to record its fix availability and deadline.

human_control_availability.HUMAN_CONTROL.what: A control needs a second person, and this repository has only one.
human_control_availability.HUMAN_CONTROL.why: The control cannot exist here; it is recorded as unvalidated.
human_control_availability.HUMAN_CONTROL.fix: Name an approver from platform or security outside the team (docs/adoption/ROLLOUT_PLAN.md, small teams).

human_control_availability.HUMAN_CONTROL.what: Two people can review each other here, but nobody independent approves exceptions.
human_control_availability.HUMAN_CONTROL.fix: Use an approver from platform or security for exceptions and uat/prod.

deployment_outcome.DEPLOY_REFUSED.what: The deploy was refused before it changed anything; the reason is the first refusal listed below it.
deployment_outcome.DEPLOY_REFUSED.why: Nothing in the environment was touched, so there is nothing to clean up.
deployment_outcome.DEPLOY_REFUSED.fix: Read the refusal named in the deploy summary (each has its own entry in this catalogue), fix it, and re-run the deploy.

deployment_outcome.PARTIAL_APPLY.what: The deploy started changing the environment and could not confirm it finished.
deployment_outcome.PARTIAL_APPLY.why: Things may exist that no record knows about.
deployment_outcome.PARTIAL_APPLY.fix: Do not re-run blindly: ask the platform team to inspect the target (the summary names it) before another deploy.

deployment_outcome.MANUAL_RECOVERY_REQUI.what: The deploy failed its checks and could not undo itself automatically; the failed version is still live.
deployment_outcome.MANUAL_RECOVERY_REQUI.why: A person has to decide how to recover.
deployment_outcome.MANUAL_RECOVERY_REQUI.fix: Follow the escalation in the deploy summary (owner and allowed actions), or contact the platform team now.

deployment_outcome.ROLLBACK_TO_PRIOR.what: The new version failed its checks and the deploy put the previous version back.
deployment_outcome.ROLLBACK_TO_PRIOR.why: Your change is not live; the previous version is.
deployment_outcome.ROLLBACK_TO_PRIOR.fix: Read why the new version failed (health or tests in the summary), fix it and deploy again.

deployment_outcome.ROLLBACK_PARTIAL.what: The deploy undid part of the change but not all of it.
deployment_outcome.ROLLBACK_PARTIAL.why: The environment is in a mixed state.
deployment_outcome.ROLLBACK_PARTIAL.fix: Ask the platform team to review the residue listed in the summary before deploying again.

deployment_outcome.STATUS_UNTRUSTED.what: The deploy changed the environment and then lost track of what it changed.
deployment_outcome.STATUS_UNTRUSTED.why: Nobody knows the current state; it is neither success nor clean failure.
deployment_outcome.STATUS_UNTRUSTED.fix: Stop deploying to this target and ask the platform team to inspect it.

rollback_capability.UNAVAILABLE.what: If this deploy failed, it could not be undone (no usable previous version or no reversal mechanism).
rollback_capability.UNAVAILABLE.why: At uat and prod a deploy that cannot be undone is refused.
rollback_capability.UNAVAILABLE.fix: Enable multiple revisions (Container Apps) or a staging slot (App Service), or keep the previous artefact; then re-run.

previous_state.UNKNOWN.what: The deploy could not read what was running before it, so it did not change anything.
previous_state.UNKNOWN.why: Without a known starting point, a safe rollback is impossible.
previous_state.UNKNOWN.fix: Re-run; if it repeats, check the deploy identity can read the target (Reader on its resource group).

rollback_state.ROLLBACK_REQUIRES_VALIDAT.what: The change can be undone, but the restored state must be proven correct before anyone calls it done.
rollback_state.ROLLBACK_REQUIRES_VALIDAT.why: A rollback that exits 0 is not a working service.
rollback_state.ROLLBACK_REQUIRES_VALIDAT.fix: Watch the verification in the summary; if it fails, escalate to the platform team.

rollback_state.ROLLBACK_REQUIRES_HUMAN_D.what: Undoing this change needs a person to decide: the previous state is unknown or reversal has consequences.
rollback_state.ROLLBACK_REQUIRES_HUMAN_D.why: A machine should not weigh those consequences.
rollback_state.ROLLBACK_REQUIRES_HUMAN_D.fix: Contact the platform team with the run link; do not re-run the deploy.

rollback_state.ROLLBACK_PROHIBITED.what: This change must not be undone; it can only be fixed forward.
rollback_state.ROLLBACK_PROHIBITED.why: Reversing it would be worse than the failure (for example a data migration).
rollback_state.ROLLBACK_PROHIBITED.fix: Fix forward: correct the code and deploy a new version.

attestation_verification.ATTESTATION_ABS.what: No signed build record (attestation) exists for this image.
attestation_verification.ATTESTATION_ABS.why: Nobody can prove where the image came from; advisory at crawl, a decision above it.
attestation_verification.ATTESTATION_ABS.fix: Build the image through the kit's build workflow (it signs every image) instead of pushing it by hand.

attestation_verification.ATTESTATION_CON.what: The image's signed build record does not match (wrong signature, image, builder or type).
attestation_verification.ATTESTATION_CON.why: This may mean the image was tampered with; it always blocks.
attestation_verification.ATTESTATION_CON.fix: Do not deploy it. Rebuild from main through the kit's build workflow and tell AppSec about the mismatch.

attestation_verification.ATTESTATION_NOT.what: The image's signed build record could not be checked (the service was unreachable or the verifier missing).
attestation_verification.ATTESTATION_NOT.why: An unchecked signature is not a pass.
attestation_verification.ATTESTATION_NOT.fix: Re-run; if it persists, check the runner can reach the GitHub attestations API.

attestation_verification.ATTESTATION_HEL.what: This private repository's GitHub plan does not offer attestations, so the signature check was skipped.
attestation_verification.ATTESTATION_HEL.why: It is recorded as a known gap of the plan, not a failure.
attestation_verification.ATTESTATION_HEL.fix: Nothing for you. On Enterprise Cloud, set the repository variable ATTESTATIONS_AVAILABLE to true.

environment_protection.ENVIRONMENT_REVIE.what: The uat or prod environment has no required reviewers (no required-reviewers rule), so anyone who can run the workflow could deploy.
environment_protection.ENVIRONMENT_REVIE.why: A production deploy must be approved by someone other than the deployer; the deploy is refused.
environment_protection.ENVIRONMENT_REVIE.fix: A repository admin adds required reviewers (platform or security) in Settings > Environments > <env>; .kit/ADOPTION_CHECKLIST.md has the gh api command.

environment_protection.ENVIRONMENT_REVIE.what: The uat or prod environment has a required-reviewers rule that names nobody, so nobody is waited for.
environment_protection.ENVIRONMENT_REVIE.why: A production deploy needs a person from platform or security to approve it; the deploy is refused before sign-in.
environment_protection.ENVIRONMENT_REVIE.fix: A repository admin adds the platform or security team as a required reviewer in Settings > Environments > <env>; .kit/ADOPTION_CHECKLIST.md has the exact gh api -X PUT command.

environment_protection.ENVIRONMENT_NOT_F.what: The uat or prod environment this deploy names does not exist in the repository.
environment_protection.ENVIRONMENT_NOT_F.why: Without the environment GitHub has no reviewer to wait for, so a production deploy would need no approval; it is refused before sign-in.
environment_protection.ENVIRONMENT_NOT_F.fix: Create the environment with its reviewers (the gh api -X PUT repos/<repo>/environments/<env> command in .kit/ADOPTION_CHECKLIST.md), or correct the github_environment name in the caller workflow.

environment_protection.ENVIRONMENT_UNCLA.what: The deploy names no environment, or one the kit cannot tell is dev, test, uat or prod.
environment_protection.ENVIRONMENT_UNCLA.why: An environment nobody has classed might be production, so it is refused at every tier rather than deployed without an approval.
environment_protection.ENVIRONMENT_UNCLA.fix: Add the environment to .kit/environments.json with "class": "dev", "test", "uat" or "prod" (kit init writes this file), or use a name with dev, test, uat or prod in it.

environment_protection.ENVIRONMENT_APPRO.what: None of the uat or prod environment's reviewers is in the platform or security approver pool.
environment_protection.ENVIRONMENT_APPRO.why: Approvals for production come from platform or security, outside the app team; the deploy is refused before sign-in.
environment_protection.ENVIRONMENT_APPRO.fix: Make a platform or security pool team (vars.KIT_APPROVER_POOLS, else approver_pools in .kit/settings.json) a required reviewer of the environment in Settings > Environments > <env>.

environment_protection.ENVIRONMENT_APPRO.what: Every reviewer of the uat or prod environment is on the app team that wrote the change.
environment_protection.ENVIRONMENT_APPRO.why: The team cannot approve its own production release; someone from platform or security must be able to; the deploy is refused before sign-in.
environment_protection.ENVIRONMENT_APPRO.fix: Add the platform or security team as a required reviewer of the environment (Settings > Environments > <env>), keeping Prevent self-review on.

environment_protection.ENVIRONMENT_SELF_.what: The environment lets the person who started the deploy approve it themselves.
environment_protection.ENVIRONMENT_SELF_.why: Self-approval is not an independent check; the deploy is refused.
environment_protection.ENVIRONMENT_SELF_.fix: Tick "Prevent self-review" in Settings > Environments > <env> (or prevent_self_review: true in the gh api call).

environment_protection.ENVIRONMENT_APPRO.what: The environment's reviewers are not from the approver groups the policy names.
environment_protection.ENVIRONMENT_APPRO.why: Someone outside the named groups could approve a production release; refused.
environment_protection.ENVIRONMENT_APPRO.fix: Set the environment's required reviewers to the groups the summary names (for example platform or security).

environment_protection.ENVIRONMENT_PROTE.what: The deploy could not read the environment's protection rules (or the tier is not registered).
environment_protection.ENVIRONMENT_PROTE.why: Unknown protection is not protection; refused at uat and prod.
environment_protection.ENVIRONMENT_PROTE.fix: Check the deploy job has actions: read and that KIT_ENVIRONMENT_TIER is one of sandbox, dev, test, uat, prod.

release_block.RELEASE_BLOCKED_BY_PLATFOR.what: The landing zone has paused releases to this workload (halted, expired, or over budget).
release_block.RELEASE_BLOCKED_BY_PLATFOR.why: Releases resume only when the platform lifts the stop; nothing was deployed.
release_block.RELEASE_BLOCKED_BY_PLATFOR.fix: Ask the platform team why (the summary shows the value of KIT_RELEASE_BLOCK); do not change the variable yourself.

zone_readiness.READY_WITH_EXCEPTIONS.what: The landing zone is ready with recorded exceptions; uat and prod releases proceed with a warning.
zone_readiness.READY_WITH_EXCEPTIONS.why: Some readiness checks have approved exceptions.
zone_readiness.READY_WITH_EXCEPTIONS.fix: Nothing for you; the platform team owns the exceptions.

zone_readiness.NOT_READY.what: The landing zone for this environment failed a readiness check.
zone_readiness.NOT_READY.why: The zone may take nothing beyond dev until it is fixed.
zone_readiness.NOT_READY.fix: Ask the platform team which readiness gate failed.

zone_readiness.UNKNOWN.what: Nobody has established whether the landing zone is ready (the value is unset or unrecognised).
zone_readiness.UNKNOWN.why: uat and prod releases are refused until it is known.
zone_readiness.UNKNOWN.fix: Inside a landing zone, ask the platform team to vend KIT_ZONE_READINESS; outside one, AppSec writes .kit/zone-readiness.json.

zone_readiness_gate.RELEASE_REFUSED_ZONE.what: A uat or prod release was refused because the target zone is not ready, or its readiness is unknown.
zone_readiness_gate.RELEASE_REFUSED_ZONE.why: Production releases need a zone that passed its readiness checks.
zone_readiness_gate.RELEASE_REFUSED_ZONE.fix: Inside a landing zone, ask the platform team; outside one, AppSec adds .kit/zone-readiness.json (docs/adoption/ZONE_READINESS_ATTESTATION.md).

readiness_source.READINESS_ATTESTATION_R.what: The readiness attestation file exists, but one of its checks failed (expired, wrong environment, or not approved by AppSec).
readiness_source.READINESS_ATTESTATION_R.why: Only a valid AppSec attestation lets a repository outside a landing zone reach uat or prod.
readiness_source.READINESS_ATTESTATION_R.fix: Ask AppSec to correct .kit/zone-readiness.json (the summary names the failed check) and approve it in a pull request.

readiness_source.READINESS_SOURCE_SELF_S.what: KIT_ZONE_READINESS was set by the deploying team itself, with no landing-zone marker and no AppSec attestation.
readiness_source.READINESS_SOURCE_SELF_S.why: A team cannot certify its own platform; refused at uat and prod.
readiness_source.READINESS_SOURCE_SELF_S.fix: Delete the variable you set; ask AppSec for .kit/zone-readiness.json instead.

readiness_source.READINESS_SOURCE_TEST_F.what: The readiness value is a labelled test fixture, not a real readiness.
readiness_source.READINESS_SOURCE_TEST_F.why: Allowed for testing, never an issued readiness.
readiness_source.READINESS_SOURCE_TEST_F.fix: Nothing in a test repository; remove KIT_ZONE_READINESS_TEST_FIXTURE in a real one.

readiness_source.READINESS_NOT_SET.what: No readiness is set and there is no attestation file.
readiness_source.READINESS_NOT_SET.why: uat and prod releases are refused until readiness is established.
readiness_source.READINESS_NOT_SET.fix: Inside a landing zone, the platform team vends it; outside one, AppSec writes .kit/zone-readiness.json.

release_approval.RELEASE_APPROVAL_ABSENT.what: Nobody approved this production deploy (an admin bypassed the review, or the environment has no reviewers).
release_approval.RELEASE_APPROVAL_ABSENT.why: A uat or prod release needs a recorded approval by someone else; refused.
release_approval.RELEASE_APPROVAL_ABSENT.fix: Re-run the deploy and ask a reviewer from platform or security to approve it in the run page (Review deployments).

release_approval.SELF_DEPLOYMENT_APPROVA.what: The person who approved this release is the one who requested it, or the author of the change.
release_approval.SELF_DEPLOYMENT_APPROVA.why: Approving your own release is never accepted.
release_approval.SELF_DEPLOYMENT_APPROVA.fix: Re-run and have a reviewer who is neither the requester nor the author approve it.

release_approval.RELEASE_APPROVAL_NOT_BO.what: The approval did not quote the image digest being released, so it is not shown to be for these exact bytes.
release_approval.RELEASE_APPROVAL_NOT_BO.why: Production approvals must name what they approve.
release_approval.RELEASE_APPROVAL_NOT_BO.fix: Re-run and approve with a comment that contains the digest (or its first 12 hex characters); the summary shows it under "For the approver".

release_approval.RELEASE_APPROVAL_NOT_ES.what: The deploy could not read who approved it, who requested it or who wrote the change.
release_approval.RELEASE_APPROVAL_NOT_ES.why: An approval nobody can read is not an approval; refused.
release_approval.RELEASE_APPROVAL_NOT_ES.fix: Check the deploy job has actions: read and that the commit author's email is linked to a GitHub account; re-run.

version_gap_ruling.VERSION_GAP_REFUSED.what: A uat or prod deploy was refused because part of the code could not be scanned at its version, and nobody accepted that gap.
version_gap_ruling.VERSION_GAP_REFUSED.why: Production gets only code the scanners could read, or a named person's accepted exception.
version_gap_ruling.VERSION_GAP_REFUSED.fix: Upgrade to a supported version, or deploy with all five weakening fields filled in by an approver who is not you.

version_gap_ruling.ADVISORY_CAUSE_UNKNOW.what: A uat or prod deploy was given an advisory verdict without the reason for it.
version_gap_ruling.ADVISORY_CAUSE_UNKNOW.why: The deploy cannot judge an advisory it cannot read.
version_gap_ruling.ADVISORY_CAUSE_UNKNOW.fix: Pass advisory_causes from the security job to the deploy job (the template passes needs.security.outputs.advisory_causes).

verdict_provenance.TYPED_VERDICT.what: The deploy was handed a verdict that no security scan produced (it was typed in).
verdict_provenance.TYPED_VERDICT.why: A typed verdict is refused at uat and prod unless AppSec recorded a manual review.
verdict_provenance.TYPED_VERDICT.fix: Deploy from a run that ran the security scan, or have AppSec fill manual_review_by, manual_review_ref and manual_review_date.

verdict_provenance.VERDICT_CONTRADICTED.what: The verdict handed to the deploy is more permissive than what the security scan actually decided.
verdict_provenance.VERDICT_CONTRADICTED.why: A deploy cannot be told "pass" when the scan said otherwise; refused at every tier.
verdict_provenance.VERDICT_CONTRADICTED.fix: Pass the security job's own routing_result and advisory_causes to the deploy, unchanged.

verdict_provenance.VERDICT_RECORD_UNREAD.what: The deploy could not read the security scan's record for the run its verdict came from.
verdict_provenance.VERDICT_RECORD_UNREAD.why: An unreadable record is not "no record"; refused at uat and prod.
verdict_provenance.VERDICT_RECORD_UNREAD.fix: Check the security run still has its kit-security-record artifact (retention) and the deploy job has actions: read.

promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_SOURCE_.what: The run you promoted from has no readable promotion record for that environment.
promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_SOURCE_.why: Without the record nobody can show the build was tested there.
promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_SOURCE_.fix: Check promote_from_run_id and promote_from_environment name a successful test (or uat) deploy run.

promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_DIGEST_.what: The image you are promoting is not the one the earlier environment verified.
promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_DIGEST_.why: Promotion must move the exact same bytes; a substitute is refused.
promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_DIGEST_.fix: Promote by run id with the template's promote job (it reads the digest from the record); do not type a digest.

promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_WRONG_P.what: The run you promoted from deployed to the wrong environment (for example dev instead of test).
promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_WRONG_P.why: uat and prod accept only builds verified in their predecessor.
promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_WRONG_P.fix: Promote from the test deploy (or uat for prod, if your policy says so).

promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_NOT_VER.what: The earlier deploy did not pass everything needed to be promoted (health, e2e tests, posture).
promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_NOT_VER.why: Only a fully tested build moves on; the summary names what was missing.
promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_NOT_VER.fix: Fix what the record lists as missing (often KIT_E2E_TEST_COMMAND is unset), redeploy to test, then promote that run.

promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_NOT_FRO.what: The build you are promoting was not built from the default branch.
promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_NOT_FRO.why: Only merged, reviewed code reaches uat and prod.
promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_NOT_FRO.fix: Merge your change to main, let it deploy to test, and promote that run.

promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_SIGNATU.what: The image's signed build record did not verify during promotion.
promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_SIGNATU.why: Production gets only images whose origin is proven.
promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_SIGNATU.fix: Rebuild through the kit's build workflow from main; see the attestation entries in this catalogue.

promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_REVOKED.what: This build was revoked (listed in the revocation register, or a new critical or known-exploited issue was found).
promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_REVOKED.why: A revoked build is never promoted.
promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_REVOKED.fix: Build and test a fixed version; the summary names the revocation reason.

promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_NEW_FIN.what: A fresh scan of the build found a high-severity issue that was not there at build time.
promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_NEW_FIN.why: New vulnerabilities are published daily; the build is no longer what was approved.
promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_NEW_FIN.fix: Upgrade the affected package, rebuild, test, and promote the new run.

promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_RECHECK.what: The re-check at promotion could not finish (SBOM scan, KEV list, history or revocations unreadable).
promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_RECHECK.why: An unfinished check is not a pass.
promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_RECHECK.fix: Re-run the promotion; if it persists, check the source run's artifacts still exist.

promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_STALE.what: The build was verified more than 14 days ago.
promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_STALE.why: Old builds miss newer fixes and findings.
promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_STALE.fix: Deploy a fresh build to test and promote that one (or record a rollback/hotfix decision).

promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_SUPERSE.what: A newer build has been verified in the same environment since this one.
promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_SUPERSE.why: Promoting an older build would skip the newer one.
promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_SUPERSE.fix: Promote the newest verified run instead.

promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_NO_PRED.what: A uat or prod deploy named no run to promote from.
promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_NO_PRED.why: uat and prod are only promoted, never built for.
promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_NO_PRED.fix: Dispatch the workflow with promote_from_run_id (the test deploy run) and promote_from_environment.

promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_PATH_UN.what: release_path is not one of normal, hotfix, rollback or break-glass.
promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_PATH_UN.why: The deploy cannot pick rules for an unknown path.
promotion_gate.PROMOTION_REFUSED_PATH_UN.fix: Set release_path to normal (or hotfix, rollback, break-glass with an exception record).

promotion_gate.DAST_REFUSED_PRODUCTION_T.what: Active DAST (attack testing) was configured against prod.
promotion_gate.DAST_REFUSED_PRODUCTION_T.why: DAST runs against the environment before prod, never prod itself.
promotion_gate.DAST_REFUSED_PRODUCTION_T.fix: Leave dast_command empty for prod (the template already does).

promotion_gate.TEST_PERIOD_REFUSED_OUT_O.what: The end-to-end test period is not between 1 and 240 minutes.
promotion_gate.TEST_PERIOD_REFUSED_OUT_O.why: A test period must be real and bounded.
promotion_gate.TEST_PERIOD_REFUSED_OUT_O.fix: Set e2e_test_period_minutes to a value from 1 to 240.

promotion_gate.BREAK_GLASS_REFUSED_NO_EX.what: An emergency (break-glass) release was requested without a reason, authority, ticket and expiry.
promotion_gate.BREAK_GLASS_REFUSED_NO_EX.why: Break-glass is allowed only with a full exception record.
promotion_gate.BREAK_GLASS_REFUSED_NO_EX.fix: Fill exception_reason, exception_authority, exception_approver, exception_ref and exception_expires.

promotion_gate.BREAK_GLASS_REFUSED_EXPIR.what: The break-glass exception's expiry date has passed.
promotion_gate.BREAK_GLASS_REFUSED_EXPIR.why: An expired emergency approval is not an approval.
promotion_gate.BREAK_GLASS_REFUSED_EXPIR.fix: Get a new exception with a future expiry (at most 7 days).

promotion_gate.BREAK_GLASS_REFUSED_TOO_L.what: The break-glass exception expires more than 7 days out.
promotion_gate.BREAK_GLASS_REFUSED_TOO_L.why: Emergency exceptions are short by rule.

promotion_revocation.DIGEST_REVOKED.what: This exact image is on the revocation list.
promotion_revocation.DIGEST_REVOKED.why: A revoked image is never promoted.
promotion_revocation.DIGEST_REVOKED.fix: Build, test and promote a new version.

promotion_revocation.SIGNING_IDENTITY_RE.what: The build workflow that signed this image has been revoked.
promotion_revocation.SIGNING_IDENTITY_RE.why: Nothing it signed is trusted any more.
promotion_revocation.SIGNING_IDENTITY_RE.fix: Rebuild with the current kit build workflow and promote the new run.

promotion_revocation.APPROVAL_REVOKED.what: An approval behind the earlier deploy was revoked.
promotion_revocation.APPROVAL_REVOKED.fix: Redeploy to the predecessor with a fresh approval, then promote.

promotion_revocation.TEST_EVIDENCE_INVAL.what: The test results behind this build were declared invalid.
promotion_revocation.TEST_EVIDENCE_INVAL.fix: Re-run the tests by redeploying to test, then promote that run.

promotion_revocation.NEW_KNOWN_EXPLOITED.what: A package in this build is now on the known-exploited vulnerability list.
promotion_revocation.NEW_KNOWN_EXPLOITED.fix: Upgrade the package, rebuild and promote the new run.

promotion_revocation.NEW_CRITICAL_FINDIN.what: A fresh scan found a critical vulnerability the build did not have before.
promotion_revocation.NEW_CRITICAL_FINDIN.fix: Upgrade the package, rebuild and promote the new run.

promotion_check.DAST_BLOCKING_FINDINGS.what: The attack test (DAST) found an error-level issue in the running app.
promotion_check.DAST_BLOCKING_FINDINGS.why: The build is not marked tested, so it cannot be promoted.
promotion_check.DAST_BLOCKING_FINDINGS.fix: Read the DAST SARIF in the deploy evidence, fix the issue, redeploy.

promotion_check.DAST_INCOMPLETE.what: The attack test (DAST) left no readable report.
promotion_check.DAST_INCOMPLETE.why: An unfinished test is never a pass.
promotion_check.DAST_INCOMPLETE.fix: Check KIT_DAST_COMMAND writes SARIF to $PROMOTION_DAST_SARIF and finishes within 30 minutes.

promotion_check.POSTURE_FAILED.what: A security setting on the running app does not hold (the summary names it).
promotion_check.POSTURE_FAILED.why: The app is live with a weaker setting than required.
promotion_check.POSTURE_FAILED.fix: Fix the named setting (for example HTTPS only, minimum TLS) in your infrastructure code and redeploy.

promotion_check.POSTURE_UNREADABLE.what: The deploy could not read the running app's security settings.
promotion_check.POSTURE_UNREADABLE.why: An unreadable setting is not a passing one.
promotion_check.POSTURE_UNREADABLE.fix: Check the deploy identity can read the target (Reader); re-run.

target_lease.LEASE_HELD.what: Another pipeline (the landing zone or another run) is changing this target right now.
target_lease.LEASE_HELD.why: Two writers at once could break it; this deploy stopped before changing anything.
target_lease.LEASE_HELD.fix: Wait for the other run to finish (the summary names it) and re-run.

target_lease.STALE_LEASE_HOLDER.what: This run's hold on the target was taken over or broken, so its change was not sent.
target_lease.STALE_LEASE_HOLDER.why: Another writer owns the target now.
target_lease.STALE_LEASE_HOLDER.fix: Re-run the deploy once the target is free.

target_lease.LEASE_EXPIRED_HOLDER.what: This run's hold on the target expired, so its change was not sent.
target_lease.LEASE_EXPIRED_HOLDER.why: Another writer could take over at any moment.

target_lease.LEASE_ABANDONED_MID_MUTATIO.what: A previous run stopped in the middle of changing this target.
target_lease.LEASE_ABANDONED_MID_MUTATIO.why: The target's state is unknown; a person must decide before anyone deploys.
target_lease.LEASE_ABANDONED_MID_MUTATIO.fix: Contact the platform team (the break authority) with the run link.

target_lease.RELEASE_MID_MUTATION.what: A run tried to let go of the target while still changing it; refused.
target_lease.RELEASE_MID_MUTATION.why: The hold never reads clean over a half-done change.
target_lease.RELEASE_MID_MUTATION.fix: Contact the platform team with the run link.

target_lease.BREAK_NOT_AUTHORISED.what: Someone outside the break authority tried to break the target's hold.
target_lease.BREAK_NOT_AUTHORISED.why: Only the named break authority may do that, with a recorded reason.
target_lease.BREAK_NOT_AUTHORISED.fix: Ask the break authority (platform team) to do it.

target_lease.LEASE_STORE_UNREACHABLE.what: The deploy could not reach the store that coordinates deploys to this target.
target_lease.LEASE_STORE_UNREACHABLE.why: It fails closed: nothing was changed.
target_lease.LEASE_STORE_UNREACHABLE.fix: Run on a runner that reaches the lease storage account (runner_label), or ask the platform team; re-run.

target_lease.LEASE_TARGET_NOT_VENDED.what: The coordination record for this target does not exist; the landing zone creates it with the target.
target_lease.LEASE_TARGET_NOT_VENDED.fix: Ask the platform team to vend the target's lease container.

target_lease.LEASE_LOST.what: The deploy lost its hold on the target during a long step, so it stopped.
target_lease.LEASE_LOST.why: Continuing without the hold could collide with another writer.
target_lease.LEASE_LOST.fix: Re-run; if it repeats, the platform team checks the lease store.

target_lease.LEASE_NOT_HELD.what: The deploy tried to change the target without holding it; refused.
target_lease.LEASE_NOT_HELD.why: Coordination is on for this environment and every change must hold the target.
target_lease.LEASE_NOT_HELD.fix: Re-run the whole deploy (it takes the hold first).

target_lease.MUTATED_WITHOUT_LEASE.what: The deploy lost its hold while a change was in flight; the change may have landed.
target_lease.MUTATED_WITHOUT_LEASE.why: A person must decide whether to roll back.
target_lease.MUTATED_WITHOUT_LEASE.fix: Contact the platform team with the run link.

target_lease.MUTATION_FAILED.what: A change to the target failed while the deploy held it.
target_lease.MUTATION_FAILED.why: The target is marked as mid-change so nobody takes it over automatically.
target_lease.MUTATION_FAILED.fix: Contact the platform team with the run link.

rollback_dependency_check.DEPLOY_REFUSED.what: This deploy is built on something that was rolled back (a commit, an image or a dependency).
rollback_dependency_check.DEPLOY_REFUSED.why: Deploying it would bring back what the rollback removed.
rollback_dependency_check.DEPLOY_REFUSED.fix: Rebase onto the current main (after the rollback), rebuild and deploy; the report names each dependency.

rollback_dependency_check.ROLLBACK_DEPEN.what: The deploy could not check whether it depends on a recent rollback.
rollback_dependency_check.ROLLBACK_DEPEN.fix: Re-run; if it persists, check the deploy job has actions: read.

seam_ownership_refusal.SEAM_SETTING_OWNE.what: The deploy would change an app setting the landing zone owns (or both sides claim it).
seam_ownership_refusal.SEAM_SETTING_OWNE.why: Each setting has one owner; nothing was written.
seam_ownership_refusal.SEAM_SETTING_OWNE.fix: Remove the key from KIT_SETTING_KEYS or ask the platform team to hand it over (the summary names the key).

seam_ownership_refusal.SEAM_SWAP_MOVES_L.what: An App Service slot swap would carry a landing-zone setting from one slot to the other.
seam_ownership_refusal.SEAM_SWAP_MOVES_L.why: That would change platform configuration; the swap is refused.
